diagnosis.fault: 64 of the 256 gains of the LayerNorm in front of the last MLP (blocks.5.ln2.weight) were multiplied by a common factor of about 4.5 (weights-only estimates 4.45 to 4.51). The affected channels are scattered, not contiguous: 4, 10, 11, 17, 19, 20, 21, 23, 26, 29, 32, 35, 38, 58, 60, 63, 64, 65, 66, 67, 78, 79, 81, 83, 84, 85, 87, 89, 90, 103, 118, 119, 120, 125, 128, 130, 133, 137, 139, 143, 150, 158, 163, 164, 168, 174, 176, 184, 191, 201, 203, 204, 210, 214, 216, 219, 221, 222, 224, 226, 232, 239, 252, 254. The other 192 gains and every other tensor look undamaged.
diagnosis.evidence: Weights: the 64 gains form a separate cluster (3.86 to 5.81, mean 5.41) with an empty gap to the other 192 (0.91 to 1.35, mean 1.22, in line with the depth trend of all other LayerNorm gains); the cluster still correlates 0.93 with the column norms of blocks.5.mlp.fc.weight, so it was scaled, not replaced. Passes: damaged checkpoint 2.512 nats/token on 64 random 256-token dev windows and 2.371 on 64 whole dev stories; after dividing the 64 gains by 4.5 the same inputs give 1.674 and 1.522 (healthy reference 1.688 and 1.605 on their own samples). 4 of 20 passes used.

diagnosis.fault: The output (write) matrix of layer-5 attention head 6 was zeroed: columns 192-223 of blocks.5.attn.proj.weight are exactly 0 (8192 weights), which removes that head's whole contribution to the residual stream. Its query/key/value rows are intact. No other tensor shows damage.
diagnosis.evidence: Weights: 12.5% of blocks.5.attn.proj.weight is exactly zero, all of it in columns 192-223 and nothing else in any tensor; the matrix has rank 224 while every other attn.proj has rank 256; head 6's value rows have norm 5.43 (third largest in the layer), and in the 47 intact heads the write-matrix norm tracks the value-row norm (within about 25%), so a zero write matrix is not a trained state. Passes: damaged loss 1.7194 on 64 dev windows of 256 tokens (healthy reference 1.688) and 1.5792 on 64 whole dev stories (my sample, truncated to 256 tokens; healthy reference 1.605 on the study's sample, so not directly comparable). Captured L5 attention shows head 6 is still a working long-range content head (mean distance 41 tokens) whose pattern is closest to heads 1 and 7 (cosine 0.59, 0.57). Filling the zeroed columns with the neighbours' mean OV circuit lowered loss to 1.7131 (windows) and 1.5725 (stories): a consistent but small gain of about 0.006-0.007 nats, so the head matters and the repair is only partial.

diagnosis.fault: Dense iid Gaussian noise added to the whole attention output projection of layer 3 (all 8 heads, all 65536 entries), sigma about 0.061 (about 1.5x the estimated clean entry std of 0.041; noise Frobenius norm about 15.6 against a clean norm of about 10.5). The underlying weight is still present underneath the noise; it is not a rescale or a replacement.
diagnosis.evidence: Weights: in layers 1,2,4,5 each head's output block O_h and value block V_h are balanced (O_h^T O_h ~ V_h V_h^T, ||O_h||/||V_h|| = 0.97-1.02, column-norm correlation 0.92-0.99). Only in layer 3 the tensor norm is 18.8 instead of ~10.5, O_h^T O_h ~ 1.0*V_h V_h^T + c*I with c = 0.88-1.08 in every head (trace excess 29.2-31.4 per head, i.e. the same sigma = 0.061 everywhere), entry kurtosis 3.00, column-norm correlation with V drops to 0.46. No other tensor shows an anomaly. Passes (8 of 20 used): damaged loss 1.717 / 1.804 on two sets of 64 random dev windows and 1.672 on 64 whole stories; zeroing the tensor gives 1.729 on the first set (so the noisy tensor still carries useful signal, and layer-3 attention is a modest contributor); the Wiener-filtered repair gives 1.679 / 1.766 / 1.641 on the same three sets, a consistent gain of 0.031-0.038 nats. The healthy loss on these exact samples is unknown, so the residual gap is not measured; the noise cannot be removed exactly from the weights alone.

diagnosis.fault: A foreign rank-1 component (sigma about 36.2, roughly 12 times the tensor's next singular value of 3.10) has been added to the MLP output projection of block 2. Its output direction u is dense and random-looking, not a learned direction, so the block-2 MLP writes a large spurious vector into the residual stream at every position.
diagnosis.evidence: Weights: sigma_1 = 36.24 against 3.10, 3.05, 2.82 next and 2.4 to 4.8 for the top value of every other mlp.proj; Frobenius norm 42.2 against 18 to 27 for the others; later layers read u with norms 1.62 (L3 mlp.fc) and 1.27 (L3 qkv), which is what a random unit vector gives, against 2.2 to 3.4 for the learned directions; |v| is uncorrelated with fc row norms (0.007 against 0.12 to 0.17). Passes (4 of 20): on the same 64 dev windows loss was 1.7636 damaged and 1.6578 after removing the term; on the same 64 dev stories 1.6609 damaged and 1.5563 repaired. In the damaged model layer-2 mlp_out had rms norm 8.92 with 7.45 of it along u; repaired, 4.90, between layer 1 (3.82) and layer 3 (6.79).

diagnosis.fault: The 32 input columns owned by head 5 (columns 160-191) of block 5's attention output projection were multiplied by one scalar of about 5.5 (weights-only estimate 5.56, plausible range 5.4-5.8), so this head writes about 5.5 times too strongly into the residual stream. Its direction structure is intact; only the gain is wrong.
diagnosis.evidence: Weights: head 5's columns have Frobenius norm 22.43 against 4.1-6.5 for the other heads of the layer; |O_h|/|V_h| is 5.66 for this head and 0.97-1.05 for every other head in blocks 2-5; the ratio is uniform over the head's 32 columns (5.52-5.81) and the Gram matrices O^T O and V V^T keep the usual cosine (0.971), which means a pure scalar gain, not noise. No other tensor shows an outlier. Passes (5 of 20 used): on the damaged checkpoint head 5 of block 5 writes vectors of mean norm 11.07 against 1.9-3.0 for the other heads; loss 1.845 on 64 dev windows and 1.742 on 64 whole stories. After dividing those columns by 5.556: head norm 1.99, loss 1.762 on the same windows and 1.661 on the same stories; a fresh independent draw of 64 windows gives 1.694 (standard error about 0.05), in line with the healthy 1.688.
